```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

`nis_comorbidity()` uses the optional `medicalcoder` package to apply its
AHRQ Elixhauser ICD-10-CM mapping. easyNIS does not distribute clinical code
lists. This computation is experimental and its assumptions need scientific
review.

## Score a collected cohort

The function accepts a collected data frame with `I10_DX1`, `I10_DX2`, and
other diagnosis columns.

```{r comorbidity, eval=rlang::is_installed("medicalcoder", version = "0.10.0")}
discharges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  dplyr::filter(AGE >= 18) |>
  dplyr::select(AGE, dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX"), dplyr::starts_with("DXPOA")) |>
  dplyr::collect()
scored <- nis_comorbidity(discharges)
head(scored[c("AGE", "cmrb_n", "cmrb_any")])
```

The added columns report the number of flagged conditions and whether any
were flagged. Values are computed from invented codes. Rows without usable
ICD-10 codes have missing results rather than “no comorbidity.”

## Add scores after design construction

If an analysis uses `nis_design()`, keep diagnosis columns in the design and
pass the design to `nis_comorbidity()`. Diagnosis and POA selections are
resolved from the query schema, so this also works when `nis` is a lazy DuckDB
query. This preserves the design object.

```{r design, eval=rlang::is_installed("medicalcoder", version = "0.10.0")}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure,
  keep = c(AGE, dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX"), dplyr::starts_with("DXPOA"))
)
scored_design <- nis_comorbidity(design)
head(scored_design$variables[c("AGE", "cmrb_n", "cmrb_any")])
```

The survey design fields remain the same while the analysis variables gain
comorbidity indicators.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - The function uses ICD-10 slots only; pre-October 2015 ICD-9 records cannot
>   be scored and receive missing values.
> - When matching diagnosis present-on-admission fields (`DXPOA1`, `DXPOA2`,
>   and so on) are available, the helper aligns them with the diagnosis slots.
>   `Y` and `W` count as present on admission; `N` and `U` do not. Other values
>   are unknown, and POA-exempt codes are handled by `medicalcoder`. If a
>   matching POA field is absent, the corresponding diagnosis is assumed
>   present to preserve behavior for years and inputs without POA fields. A
>   warning names the affected diagnosis slots; their POA-dependent
>   comorbidities may include conditions acquired in hospital. AHRQ's refined
>   software requires POA to assign 18 of 38 measures and returns missing
>   results when required POA information is unavailable ([AHRQ User Guide](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/toolssoftware/comorbidityicd10/CMR-User-Guide-v2024-1.pdf)).
>   `medicalcoder` uses an exemption mapping covering AHRQ fiscal years
>   2022–2026, with POA-exemption status consistent across those releases. It
>   does not adjust exemptions for discharge date, so exempt-code results can
>   differ slightly from AHRQ software across fiscal years.
>   As POA availability varies, results can differ between inputs with and
>   without those fields.
> - Do not assume agreement with older Stata-derived `ynel*` and `elixsum`
>   fields; definitions and versions differ.

See [`nis_comorbidity()`](../reference/nis_comorbidity.html) and
[Data notes by year](year-notes.html).
